title: Let new firms in

predict.q: Start: 4 shops; each earns a profit of 390. As more shops open, where does each shop end up in the long run?

options.s: Price = MC = lowest ATC, as in perfect competition.
options.fb: That is perfect competition. Each shop's demand slopes down, so AR can only touch AC where AC is still falling.

options.s: Profit above normal stays: each shop's product is different.
options.fb: Differentiation is not a barrier. While profit is above normal, new shops keep opening.

options.s: AR touches ATC at an output below the lowest point of ATC.
options.fb: At 10 shops AR touches AC at Q = 40 (P = 13): normal profit, to the left of the lowest AC at Q = 60.

options.s: Every shop makes a loss, and the market closes.
options.fb: Losses make shops leave, which shifts each remaining shop's demand back right. The market settles at normal profit.

task: Move the number-of-shops slider and watch each shop's AR, MR, price and profit.

target.do: Move the number-of-shops slider until profit is normal (zero), then press Check.
target.hint: Keep adding shops until profit per shop reaches zero.

takeaway: Entry continues until profit is normal, at the point where AR touches ATC to the **left** of the lowest point of ATC.
